experiment_classes.safe_compile_proof_prototype: Bounded internal experiments that can be tested without public support promotion or runtime/ABI promises.
experiment_classes.unsafe_without_formal_semantics: Ideas that remain blocked until a stronger semantics contract exists.
experiment_classes.requires_new_runtime_abi: Ideas that cannot become meaningful without a new governed runtime or ABI contract.

experiments.summary: Add non-public compile-proof fixtures that preserve source parenthesization and assert that only existing guarded reassociation paths may rewrite selected triples.
experiments.why_now: Wave 2 now has an explicit parenthesization contract and validator-backed registry to anchor the fixture set.

experiments.summary: Add narrow diagnostic fixtures around division-domain restrictions and zero-divisor-sensitive inverse surfaces without changing support claims.
experiments.why_now: Existing checker and stdlib semantics already expose guarded division-domain boundaries.

experiments.summary: Do not build a general reassociation or normalization engine until associativity, distributivity, and observation-sensitive reorderability are formalized more tightly.
experiments.why_now: Wave 2 clarified why current evidence is still too weak for safe general rewrite laws.

experiments.summary: Any promotion of hypercomplex native layout, ABI, or interop claims needs a dedicated governed runtime contract and validation lane.
experiments.why_now: Wave 2 bounded the semantic side, but runtime/ABI guarantees remain explicitly out of scope.
